title: Assistant chat command contracts
$comment: Owner contract schema named by Plans/Commands_System.md (Puppet Master Assistant Redesign Central Registration Addendum - 2026-09-03, "Naming them here does not create them"; CS-078, and CS-087 for the closure wave) for Plans/assistant-chat-design.md. Written 2026-09-27 as the companion of the wand-modules compile (ledgers pldg-20260927-005 and pldg-20260927-006; DL-126): the request/result pairs of every command whose contracts the central table points at this file, cmd.chat.goal.open_editor (GoalEditorRoute -> RouteResult), cmd.chat.composer.destination.set and cmd.chat.composer.destination.clear (ACD-462), cmd.chat.thread.regenerate_title (ACD-462, ACD-479), cmd.chat.eli5.set (ELI5ThreadOverrideRequest with the value on, off or inherit; UCC-175, ACD-484) and cmd.chat.eli5.explain_reply (ELI5ExplainReplyRequest/Result; UCC-174, CS-087, ACD-484). Where canon states only a command's meaning the shape is the minimal command envelope plus the target identity. ComposerDestination and ThreadTitleAttempt restate the fields Plans/Collaborative_Workflows.md section 4.5 and ACD-479 give them and are not new records: the record families pm.chat.composer_destination.v1 and pm.chat.thread_title_generation.v1 stay requires_central_adjudication. A definition here is a contract shape, not a handler, a catalogue registration or an admission: every command stays handler_unavailable, and cmd.chat.eli5.explain_reply stays a DL-035 candidate exclusion (WM-064). Requests and results are not records and add no storage key, EventRecord, writer, Settings key or physical family. DL-138 companion (2026-09-29): ThreadCrewAutoOverride is only the optional field projection of ACD-076 existing thread metadata; it adds no record envelope, durable family, storage key, writer or Settings value. Reopen persistence remains the existing owner's runtime obligation. DL-218 / ACD-503: the three grilling session controls below reuse the existing host, command envelope and owner state refs. They are handlerless candidates; the shapes admit no new durable family, event or writer.

assistant_chat_command_error_code.description: The shared typed owner error kinds of the Puppet Master Assistant Redesign Central Registration Addendum (Plans/Commands_System.md, 'Typed error vocabulary', CS-078). A failure stays a failure and never returns a success-shaped result.

GoalEditorRoute.description: GoalEditorRoute for cmd.chat.goal.open_editor, a navigation_wrapper (UI_Command_Catalog.md, Assistant chat composer, title and ELI5 rows; Commands_System.md central contract records). It navigates to Goal Activity Detail in edit mode from the Goal hover menu for the thread's present Goal; it is a route, not a Goal mutation (a Goal revision is cmd.chat.goal.update, owned by Plans/Goal_Runtime_System.md). The catalog states the command's meaning only, so the shape is the minimal envelope plus the thread and Goal identity. Contract shape only: handler_unavailable until admission.

RouteResult.description: RouteResult for cmd.chat.goal.open_editor. Accepted means the route to Goal Activity Detail in edit mode was opened; route success changes no Goal state. Rejected carries a typed error and opens nothing.

composer_destination_kind.description: ComposerDestination.destination_kind, closed by Plans/Collaborative_Workflows.md section 4.5 (Composer destination targeting), which owns the collaborative values.

ComposerDestination.description: The composer destination persisted with the composer buffer (record family pm.chat.composer_destination.v1, payload-semantics owner Plans/assistant-chat-design.md; fields as Plans/Collaborative_Workflows.md section 4.5 states them: destination_kind, destination_id, optional participant_id, display_label, state_generation). The stored label alone is never sufficient: dispatch revalidates the target and state_generation.

composer_destination_side_effects.description: What a destination change never does (ACD-462; Collaborative_Workflows.md section 4.5): it never creates or starts the workflow it names, never sends unsent composer input, and never clears composer text or attachments. Every member is false on every path.

ComposerDestinationSetRequest.description: ComposerDestinationSetRequest for cmd.chat.composer.destination.set (ACD-462; UCC-156 row). Binds the exact originating thread and an existing workflow, participant or Plan-revision target, which the composer chrome then names. The target is revalidated at dispatch, so changing the active tab never redirects a pending request. Contract shape only: handler_unavailable until admission.

source_surface.description: A registered source surface of the command's catalog row; the surface census is owned by Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md (Assistant chat composer, title and ELI5 family).

ComposerDestinationSetResult.description: ComposerDestinationSetResult. Accepted returns the bound destination; rejected (for example a target that can no longer accept input, stale_currentness) binds nothing and returns destination null. On every path the side_effects members are false: the workflow is not started and unsent input is neither sent nor cleared.

destination.description: The bound ComposerDestination when accepted, null when rejected (pinned by the outcome rules below).

ComposerDestinationClearRequest.description: ComposerDestinationClearRequest for cmd.chat.composer.destination.clear (UCC-156 row): returns the composer of the exact originating thread to the ordinary thread destination. Contract shape only: handler_unavailable until admission.

source_surface.description: A registered source surface of the command's catalog row; the surface census is owned by Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md (Assistant chat composer, title and ELI5 family).

ComposerDestinationClearResult.description: ComposerDestinationClearResult. Accepted means the composer is back on the ordinary thread destination (destination_cleared true); rejected clears nothing. Unsent composer text and attachments are kept on every path.

ThreadTitleAttempt.description: ThreadTitleAttempt {thread_id, attempt_id, requested_route, effective_route?, outcome, title?, at} (ACD-479): one record per automatic or explicit naming of a thread. An unavailable title model records route_unavailable and is never silently replaced by another model, so route_unavailable carries no effective_route; named carries the title.

ThreadTitleRegenerateRequest.description: ThreadTitleRegenerateRequest for cmd.chat.thread.regenerate_title (ACD-462, ACD-479; visible label Name it for me, DL-134). An explicit regeneration of the exact thread's title through the title owner, honouring the title policy and title-model availability; it is the only operation that clears thread.title_locked. Its source surfaces are the thread menu (directly under Rename) and the chat header (ACD-479). Contract shape only: handler_unavailable until admission.

ThreadTitleGenerationResult.description: ThreadTitleGenerationResult. Accepted returns the one ThreadTitleAttempt the explicit naming produced and title_locked false, because explicit regeneration clears the manual-rename lock; an explicit attempt is never user_locked. Rejected (for example precondition_failed with the policy off or the model unavailable, the states in which the control renders disabled) produces no attempt and returns attempt null.

attempt.description: The ThreadTitleAttempt when accepted, null when rejected (pinned by the outcome rules below).

eli5_override_value.description: The value ELI5ThreadOverrideRequest carries: exactly one of on, off and inherit (UCC-175, CS-087, ACD-484, DL-126). on and off set this chat's override; inherit deletes it, so the chat follows the project default, otherwise the app default. There is no toggle and no project-level value.

eli5_reply_side_effects.description: What an ELI5 switch never does (ACD-484, UCC-175, DL-126): it never re-sends, regenerates or rewrites an earlier reply, so a switch never produces a second response; a reply still streaming finishes in the style it started with. Every member is false on every path.

ELI5ThreadOverrideRequest.description: ELI5ThreadOverrideRequest for cmd.chat.eli5.set (UCC-175, CS-087, ACD-484, DL-126). It writes only this chat's override, the per-conversation setting general.interaction.chat-eli5: value on or off sets it and inherit deletes it. Its only source surfaces are eli5_sheet (Standard or Simple, Follow my usual setting, and the This chat level) and composer (the quick dot, on or off); the wand's ELI5 row only opens the sheet and never dispatches it. The project default and the app default (general.interaction.eli5-default) are Settings writes, never this command. Contract shape only: handler_unavailable until admission. DL-138/SSYS-028 persist general.interaction.eli5-default at project scope as well as app scope; adding that Settings level does not permit a scope or project-default write in this chat command.

ELI5ThreadOverrideResult.description: ELI5ThreadOverrideResult. Accepted: chat_override is the chat's override after the write, on or off, or null after inherit deleted it. The change applies from the next reply that starts (applies_from next_reply); every reply keeps the style it was written in, so side_effects are false on every path. Rejected changes nothing. After inherit, resolution reads the persisted project general.interaction.eli5-default, falling back to the app value only when no project override is stored (DL-138, SSYS-028).

explain_reply_side_effects.description: What Explain this reply simply never does (ACD-484, UCC-174, CS-087): it never changes, re-sends, regenerates or replaces the reply it explains and never changes the chat's ELI5 state. It is not an alias of cmd.chat.retry_message. Every member is false on every path.

ELI5ExplainReplyRequest.description: ELI5ExplainReplyRequest for cmd.chat.eli5.explain_reply (ACD-484, UCC-174, CS-087, DL-126). It targets one finished assistant reply by message_id and is dispatched only when the user asks, from that reply's message actions (message_chrome). One request writes at most one extra reply; a repeated request with the same idempotency key returns the first result and writes nothing more. Contract shape only: handler_unavailable until admission.

ELI5ExplainReplyResult.description: ELI5ExplainReplyResult. Accepted: the target was a finished assistant reply, and exactly one new reply was written (replies_written 1): an ordinary assistant reply at the end of the thread, written in Simple, that names and links the reply it explains (ACD-484). Refused while the target reply is still streaming: target_reply_state streaming is always rejected with precondition_failed and writes nothing. Every rejection writes no reply. side_effects are false on every path.

target_reply_state.description: The state of the targeted assistant reply at dispatch; null when no assistant reply with that message_id exists in the thread.

replies_written.description: Replies this request wrote: 1 when accepted, 0 when rejected (pinned by the outcome rules below), never more.

ThreadCrewAutoOverride.description: Field-level projection of existing ACD-076 thread metadata (DL-138), not a full thread record or a new durable family. crew_auto_override true or false overrides the project Crew Auto value; null or an absent property inherits. The existing thread owner persists it across reopen. cmd.chat.crew_auto.set with scope thread changes this field only; this shape admits no command, writer, storage key, Settings value or runtime persistence proof.

crew_auto_override.description: true/false is the explicit per-chat value; null and absence both inherit the project setting.

QuestionnaireGrillWrapUpRequest.description: DL-218 / ACD-503 wrap_up on the existing grilling host session. Host authenticates the explicit user action and validates owner revision/currentness. Never treated as an answer from an agent.

QuestionnaireGrillWrapUpResult.description: DL-218 / ACD-503: owner session outcome only. Confirm alone commits the agreement; none of the three controls starts implementation or grants authority. Replay returns the prior result.

QuestionnaireGrillConfirmRequest.description: DL-218 / ACD-503 confirm on the existing grilling host session. Host authenticates the explicit user action and validates owner revision/currentness. Never treated as an answer from an agent.

QuestionnaireGrillConfirmResult.description: DL-218 / ACD-503: owner session outcome only. Confirm alone commits the agreement; none of the three controls starts implementation or grants authority. Replay returns the prior result.

QuestionnaireGrillKeepGoingRequest.description: DL-218 / ACD-503 keep_going on the existing grilling host session. Host authenticates the explicit user action and validates owner revision/currentness. Never treated as an answer from an agent.

QuestionnaireGrillKeepGoingResult.description: DL-218 / ACD-503: owner session outcome only. Confirm alone commits the agreement; none of the three controls starts implementation or grants authority. Replay returns the prior result.

It reads current stop/authority state through owners and grants no mutation. Fresh inverse preview commitment, stop epochs and effect authority are required later by ChatMoveUndoApplyRequest. context preserves exact return.
